pages.text: "Your toothbrush, Bami! We're at the last stop. Brush, then sleep!" Mom waved it by the washroom. Bami hid beneath the sleeping-car quilt. "Too much trouble! I'll just sleep!"
Mom offered the brush, but Bami shook their head. "Can't I skip just once?" Before she blew out the little lamp, Bami was snoring. Brushing had been skipped.
During the night, Bami's mouth felt sticky and itchy. Dinner's breadcrumbs hid between their beak. "Something feels funny..." Bami opened their eyes.
Pipi, the sparrow who lived on the roof, tapped the round window. "Maybe cavity bugs got in!" Mom lifted the quilt. "They're playing tricks. Let's chase them out!" Bami peeked up.
As Mom told an imaginary story, Bami pictured purple cavity bugs rolling and giggling over white teeth inside their beak. "Those little pests were poking me!" Bami stamped their feet.
Mom whispered, "They fear toothpaste bubbles! Your brush is a sparkling sword, and the foam is magic bubbles! Brush, brush, sparkle!" Bami's eyes shone. Pipi repeated it outside.
Bami sprang up and went to the washroom. Toes gripping the brush, they added toothpaste. Up, down—fluffy bubbles! The dizzy cavity bugs ran away. "Brush, brush, sparkle!"
Bami rinsed and opened wide. Their teeth glittered like spring-night stars outside the round window. The itch was gone! Wings wide, Bami hopped. They had done it!
Now Bami knew the steps. "One, brush before the first toot! Two, brush at the last stop! Three, up and down, all over!" Next morning, Bami picked up the brush first. Pipi chirped the song.
Mom hugged Bami. "Teeth like stars!" With brushing every day, cavity bugs stayed away. Brush, brush, sparkle!
